title: The Seminar
intro: Three things to build with Claude, hands on, on your own laptop. You will not write any code. You say what you want in plain English and Claude does the work, and you leave with something you can use the next morning.

first.label: Do this first
first.title: Get your free Claude account
first.body: Fellows get Claude for Education from Stanford, free. Visiting scholars get a month of Pro reimbursed. Then sign in to it on your laptop.
first.time: Request it today: it takes a day or so

before.title: Before you come
before.lede: Three small things, best done this week. Stanford IT is closed on Thanksgiving and the day after.

items.title: Request your Stanford Claude account
items.body: It is free for fellows. Choose "Request a Claude for Education Standard account" and sign in with your SUNet ID. Mine took four hours to arrive.

items.title: Install the Claude desktop app
items.body: On the laptop you will bring. Mac or Windows.

items.title: Sign in with your Stanford account
items.body: This is the step people trip on, so here it is in full.

signin: Open the Claude app. If it's signed in to your personal account, log out first: click your name at the bottom left, then Log out.
Click "Get started" if you see it.
Click "Enter your email" and type your Stanford SUNet ID as an email address, something like jdoe@stanford.edu. You don't need a Stanford mailbox.
A "Continue with SSO" button appears under it. Click that one (not "Continue with email", not "Continue with Google").
Sign in on the Stanford page with your SUNet ID and password.

projects.title: Your own work website
projects.body: A personal page with what you are working on and an office-hours sign-up, built and put on the internet.
projects.time: 30 minutes to build, another hour to publish

projects.title: Your own paper library
projects.body: A few hundred papers on trust in a small database on your laptop, with a chat page that answers from them. And how that sits next to Consensus, Scite and Zotero.

projects.title: Your own fact checker
projects.body: Working on your book? A skill by CASBS alum John Markoff that checks every claim in a chapter and shows its sources.

tip.title: One habit worth having
tip.body: Each thing you build is a project in the Claude app. Rename it to something you will recognise and pin it. Tomorrow it is the first thing you see, and you pick up where you stopped.
